lesson_title: The Energy Monster on Your Roof
hook_text: In many homes, one appliance uses about two thirds of all the electricity. Can you guess which?
clip_script: Let's do an energy audit. Kettle: 1 unit a day. Stove: 2. Fridge: 1,5. TV: half a unit. Five LED lights: less than a quarter. And the geyser? 9 units a day. That is about two thirds of everything. Why? Heating water takes a huge amount of energy: one full tank needs about 8 units. But South Africa has some of the best sunshine on Earth. A solar water heater on the roof, facing north, uses a black panel under glass to soak up the Sun and heat the water for free. In sunny places it can do about 70 per cent of the work. For our family that saves almost R475 every month, and the system pays for itself in under three years.
visual_style: A home cut-away with each appliance lighting up by its daily units; a giant geyser bar; a sunlit roof with a solar collector and rising warm water.
pacing: Rapid audit, a pause on the geyser reveal, a sunny build to the savings payoff.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and do an energy audit of your own home.
